basics.name: Xuan Qi
basics.label: Ph.D. Student, University of Washington
basics.summary: Ph.D. student at the Paul G. Allen School of Computer Science & Engineering, University of Washington. B.Eng. from Tsinghua University IIIS (Yao Class). Research interests: self-evolving agent systems, autoresearch agents, agentic reinforcement learning, agent memory, and agent world models.

work.name: Xiaohongshu HI Lab, Pretraining Department (ACE Top Intern Program)
work.position: Recursively Self-Improving AI Agent Harness & Post-training Research Intern
highlights: Agentic test-time scaling and post-training: developed efficient test-time scaling methods to generate high-quality agent trajectories, prepared trajectory-based training data, and ran end-to-end SFT and RL post-training, with hands-on deployment, inference optimization, training, and evaluation of models exceeding 200B parameters.

AI4AI tasks and environments for pretraining improvement: built tasks and environments in which autoresearch agents propose, implement, and evaluate improvements to the pretraining of their underlying models; designed controlled experiments, fitted scaling laws to assess these changes, and conducted large-scale pretraining experiments.

Recursively self-improving autoresearch agents: built an autoresearch agent harness supporting recursive self-improvement across tasks including MLE-Bench, KernelBench, and nanoGPT, achieving competitive performance across multiple benchmarks.

work.name: Reinforce Omega (AI Agent Start-up)
highlights: Designed and iterated on AI agent workflows, including tool-use policies, tool-creation pipelines, and skill document generation/management to improve robustness and reusability.
Built context and memory management mechanisms to support long-horizon planning, error recovery, and multi-step execution across heterogeneous tools.
Contributed to the agent platform backend, including agent-friendly websites, web/GUI agent capabilities, and benchmarks for evaluating agent performance.

work.name: University of Pennsylvania, Cognitive Computation Group
highlights: Worked on the DataProphet project, analyzing cross-modal transferability of supervision signals across reasoning tasks and using these findings for real-data reweighting and synthetic-data selection.

The selected data subsets were substantially higher quality than strong baselines, so models trained under the same budget clearly outperformed them. Paper: [Demystifying Supervision Data Generalization in Multimodal LMs](https://openreview.net/forum?id=iYMZKz5BGz).

work.name: Princeton University
work.position: Wang Lab@Princeton: AI for Accelerating Invention
highlights: Co-led the development of [Alita](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.20286), a generalist agent with minimal predefinition and maximal self-evolution via dynamic Model Context Protocol (MCP) creation, which achieved top-1 performance on the GAIA benchmark.
Extended Alita to [Alita-G](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.23601), which abstracts and curates MCP tools to turn generalist agents into domain experts.

Co-first author of [A Survey of Self-Evolving Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.21046) and [Shallow Preference Signals](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.17122); contributed to [AgentDistill](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.14728).

work.name: Tsinghua University, IIIS
highlights: Developed a pointwise-mutual-information metric to value datasets and encourage honest data contributions, with theoretical analyses and experiments, in [Proper Dataset Valuation by Pointwise Mutual Information](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.18253).

work.name: Tsinghua University, IIIS
highlights: Led the data pipeline for HDI4D: A Hand-Deformable Object Interaction Dataset for Soft Body Hanging, covering data collection, annotation, and empirical model validation.

Tsinghua Q&A Forum Senior Volunteer; Three-Star Zijing Volunteer; Class Publicity Officer.
